title: Quiet T after S
kidRule: When T is squeezed between S and an ending like L-E or E-N, the T usually stays quiet, as in WHISTLE and FASTEN!
hint: We hear '/s/' in the middle, but a quiet letter is hiding right after the S. Which one?
reminder: A quiet T hides right after the S, so we write S-T.

check.question: Why can't we hear the T in WHISTLE?
check.correctAnswer: T usually stays quiet when it is squeezed between S and an ending like L-E or E-N!
distractors: Because T is always quiet in the middle of a word
Because the letter I makes the T quiet

words.def: A small tool that makes a high, loud sound when you blow into it.
words.sent: The coach blew her whistle to start the race.
words.story: Every dolphin makes its own special whistle sound, which works a bit like a name!
words.card: The pirate lost *his* *whistle*, so he had to squeak like a mouse!

words.def: To close or join something so that it stays in place.
words.sent: Remember to fasten your seat belt in the car.
words.story: Velcro was invented after a man noticed prickly seeds sticking to his dog's fur!
words.card: *Fasten* your helmet *fast*, the snail race is about to begin!

words.def: To make a soft, crackly sound, like dry leaves moving.
words.sent: The leaves rustle when the wind blows.
words.story: Aspen trees have flat leaf stems, so their leaves shake and whisper in even the tiniest breeze!
words.card: The *rust*y robot heard the leaves *rustle* and hid behind a pumpkin!

words.def: To snuggle into a cozy, comfy spot.
words.sent: The puppies nestle together in their warm basket.
words.story: Emperor penguin chicks snuggle on top of their parent's feet to stay warm on the ice!
words.card: Baby birds *nestle* in a *nest* made of spaghetti!

words.def: To make something a little bit wet.
words.sent: Moisten the sponge before you wipe the table.
words.story: Dogs lick their noses to keep them damp, because a damp nose is better at catching smells!
words.card: It took *ten* raindrops to *moisten* the elephant's toenail!

words.def: To bump and push against others in a crowd.
words.sent: Please do not jostle the people in line.
words.story: Emperor penguins crowd together in huge huddles to stay warm, and they keep shuffling so everyone gets a turn in the cozy middle!
words.card: *Jo*lly penguins *jostle* for the best spot on the iceberg!

words.def: To move or work fast with lots of energy.
words.sent: We had to hustle to catch the school bus.
words.story: In sports, coaches shout this word when they want players to move quickly and try their hardest!
words.card: '*Hustle*!' the turtle told *us*. 'I am winning the race!'

words.def: A prickly wild plant with purple flowers.
words.sent: A bee landed on the purple thistle.
words.story: This prickly purple plant is the national flower of Scotland!
words.card: Do not sit on *this* *thistle*, unless you want a prickly bottom!

words.def: A short, stiff hair, like the ones on a brush.
words.sent: One bristle fell out of my toothbrush.
words.story: Long ago, the stiff hairs on toothbrushes came from hogs!
words.card: This *bristle* *is* so ticklish that my toothbrush giggles!

words.def: To shine with little sparkles, like something wet.
words.sent: The snow began to glisten in the morning sun.
words.story: Fresh snow sparkles because its tiny ice crystals bounce sunlight around like little mirrors!
words.card: My shopping *list* began to *glisten* after the snail walked across it!
